fix_note: Crisis lens export surfaced only incident reports: crisis state lives in per-user globalThis._concordSTATE stores (resources/teams/timelines), which the export's artifact leg cannot see, and no export provider was registered for the domain. crisis.js now registers a lens export provider (the established calendar/achievements pattern) enumerating the caller's declared crises (identified by the server-stamped declarer timeline events, read from world_crises), their own resource inventory, and the responder rosters of crises they declared or staff — responder names are the stored display strings, and the assigner's raw id is emitted only through the file's own public label (name + isMe), never raw. Caller-scoped throughout; anonymous callers export nothing. Behaviour suite server/tests/crisis-export-provider.test.js 4/4 (pristine file fails the two positive pins). First B9 record under the per-seat append regime (founder ruling 2026-11-12).

Genesis lens export omitted saved searches: they live in STATE.genesisSavedSearches, a top-level per-user state key the export's state leg never reads (it reads STATE.<domain>Lens bags only), and no export provider was registered for the domain. genesis.js now registers a lens export provider (the established calendar/crisis pattern) emitting the caller's own saved searches with their filters. Caller-scoped; anonymous callers export nothing. Behaviour suite server/tests/genesis-export-provider.test.js 4/4 (pristine file fails the two positive pins). Landing note: the fix commit was pushed in an attempt whose session died mid-approval-wait on 2026-11-13 and was settled as landed by blob read-back (domain + test blobs match staging) at head c3124d11a during the founder's re-fire window; this record row follows the verified landing.

Society lens export said 'Nothing to export' over the lens's own records: saved charts live in STATE.societyCharts (a share-id registry, not a STATE.societyLens bag) and the agent schedules the autonomy tab's AgentBuilder manages live in STATE.agentsLens.schedules — neither is a store the shared export's legs read, and no export provider was registered for the domain. society.js now registers a lens export provider emitting the caller's own charts (ownership checked per record, exactly as wb-list-charts checks it) and the caller's agent schedules. Caller-scoped throughout; anonymous callers export nothing. Behaviour suite server/tests/society-export-provider.test.js 4/4 (pristine file fails the two positive pins). The fix was three-way merged over a concurrent wb-delete-chart addition on the shared branch; that work is preserved beside the provider.

LFG lens export said 'Nothing to export yet' over the caller's own open request: requests are rows in the lfg_requests table — not artifacts and not STATE — so no export leg could see them and no provider was registered for the domain. domains/lfg.js now registers a lens export provider emitting the caller's own OPEN, unexpired requests, projecting the same fields listOpenLfg projects; the requester's raw id is never an export field (the lib's identity-display rule). Caller-scoped; nothing exports without a caller or a db. Behaviour suite server/tests/lfg-export-provider.test.js 4/4 against a hermetic node:sqlite table mirroring migration 219 (pristine file fails the two positive pins; expired, matched and other users' requests are all excluded by the pins).

Global lens export said 'Nothing to export yet' over a saved view the lens itself had just persisted: saved views live in STATE.globalSavedViews (savedViewStore, a per-user Map) — a top-level state key the export's state leg never reads (it reads STATE.<domain>Lens bags only) — and no export provider was registered for the domain. global.js now registers a lens export provider emitting the caller's own saved views with mode, config and share link — the same list listViews returns. Caller-scoped; anonymous callers export nothing. Behaviour suite server/tests/global-export-provider.test.js 4/4 (pristine file fails the two positive pins). This is the server-scope fix for the id B6's CB-0451 recon routed to the desk, built under B9's CB-0442 claim.

Concord-Link-Frontier export excluded the lens's Link panel records, so JSON/CSV came back empty over links the user had saved: links live in the domain's own stores (the STATE.concordLinkFrontier.links in-memory bucket backed by the concord_link_frontier_links table) — neither read by the shared export's legs, and no provider was registered. concord-link-frontier.js now registers a lens export provider that reuses the domain's own merged read (orderedLinks: bucket + table, caller-scoped) and emits the caller's links with bearing and mark. Anonymous callers export nothing. Behaviour suite server/tests/clf-export-provider.test.js 4/4, including the table-hydration case (pristine file fails the two positive pins).

Move Builder header export said 'Nothing to export yet' over the caller's minted moves: a mint persists only as a row in the legacy dtus table (type='move_recipe', creator_id=caller, meta JSON in data) and never enters the platform DTU read model — dtu/list reads the separate dtu-store corpus, so the export's DTU leg can never return a minted move (and the move's kind marker sits at meta.kind, which the domain matcher never reads). move-builder.js now registers a lens export provider reading the same table its own list macro reads, in both detected shapes (runtime type/creator_id/data; minimal body_json/owner_user_id), emitting the caller's moves with element, skill kind, tier, allocation and motion. Caller-scoped; nothing exports without a caller or a db. Behaviour suite server/tests/move-builder-export-provider.test.js 4/4 against a hermetic node:sqlite dtus table (pristine file fails the two positive pins; other users' moves and non-move DTUs excluded by the pins). Distinct from FIX-move-builder-006 (the FE control-mount ticket, not in this claim).

Plugins lens export offered JSON/CSV but downloaded nothing: the lens is a REST gallery (server/lib/plugin-gallery.js), not a lens domain — the catalogue is shared platform content, and the caller's own records (their installs and ratings) live in the lib's module-private maps (_installs, _votes) that no export leg can see, behind no domain module that could register a provider. plugin-gallery.js now registers a lens export provider where the records live, emitting the caller's installs and ratings joined with the gallery entries (name, version, author); the stores keep no timestamps, so rows carry none rather than an invented one. Caller-scoped; anonymous callers export nothing. Behaviour suite server/tests/plugins-export-provider.test.js 4/4 (pristine file fails the two positive pins; another user's installs and ratings excluded by the pins).

Entity lens export filled its rows with the shared Registry's artifacts while the caller's own spawned entities never appeared: own entities are entity DTUs whose only tag is machine.kind 'entity-node'/'entity-schema' — no domain, no meta.lens (lib/entity-substrate.js nodeToDtu) — so the export's DTU leg drops them twice (the list macro's domain filter and the export's membership check both require domain or kind === the domain name). entity.js now registers a lens export provider emitting the caller's own nodes and schemas through the substrate's owner-scoped reads (listNodes/listSchemas over STATE.dtus), with entity type, attributes and Wikidata id. Cap leg, per the CB-0442 rider, discharged as far as code evidence carries it: collectLensExport applies its limit per leg and merges uncapped, so provider rows are never crowded out by the artifact leg's 1,000 rows — the provider emits the caller's full set up to the workbench's own caps (5,000 nodes / 200 schemas), which is the full export for own records. Edges are typed relations on the node DTUs, not standalone records, so they are not separate rows. Caller-scoped; anonymous callers export nothing. Behaviour suite server/tests/entity-export-provider.test.js 4/4 (pristine file fails the two positive pins).

Template Import in the Agents lens recorded a permanent per-user install count and created nothing: the server's importTemplate built a full agentDefinition (and already accepted a name), but TemplatesPanel discarded the definition and showed a success note pointing at a roster step that does not exist. The panel now persists the returned definition through the same artifact store the Fleet view creates agents in (POST /api/lens/agents, type 'agent'), under a name typed on the template card; the banner truthfully states the agent is in the Fleet roster and offers Undo, which deletes the created artifact and calls the new agents.uninstallTemplate action to reverse the caller's install count (floor 0, caller-scoped). A failed artifact save surfaces an honest error instead of a false success. Behaviour suites: server/tests/agents-template-import.test.js 4/4 and concord-frontend/tests/components/AgentRuntimeTemplates.test.tsx 2/2; both pristine files fail their positive pins.

The .dtu personal pack had no round trip: every lens's .dtu button downloads a real binary DTU (POST /api/lens/:domain/export-dtu) and the server validates and imports that exact format at POST /api/lens/:domain/import-dtu (inspectDTU), but no surface called the import — the Export Toolkit's only file-in panel was Decrypt. The toolkit gains an ImportDtuPanel (beside DecryptedArchive): pick a .dtu file, name its lens (the file's own recorded domain is preserved server-side on the created DTU), and the file posts as octet-stream to the import route, which validates it before creating anything. A file under the server's own 48-byte floor is refused client-side with no request; server rejections surface their error instead of a false success; a confirmed import reports the created DTU id. Behaviour suite concord-frontend/tests/export-toolkit-import-dtu.test.tsx 3/3 (pristine toolkit fails all three; the sibling DecryptedArchive suite still passes 4/4).

PDF/delta/enc export history entries could never be re-downloaded: the history store (export.record-run) already supported a retained payload and the desk panel's text formats already used it, but the three toolkit panels recorded their runs without the payload they had just downloaded. IncrementalExport now records the exact JSON payload it downloads (and its history filename now matches the downloaded one), EncryptedArchive records the exact envelope string (filename likewise unified), and PdfExport records the generated PDF as base64 with payloadEncoding 'base64' — ExportHistory's re-download decodes base64 payloads back to bytes and downloads utf8 payloads as before. Entries that genuinely retain nothing (pre-fix runs, scheduled bookkeeping runs) now show a clear sentence — 'No file retained for this run — re-run the export to download it again' — instead of the bare 'no payload retained' jargon, which is the EXPECTED's second arm for those entries. Behaviour suite concord-frontend/tests/export-toolkit-history-redownload.test.tsx 4/4 (pristine toolkit fails all four; DecryptedArchive + ImportDtuPanel suites unaffected).

The World Creator manifest promises an export (macros.export, exports ['json']) and the universal lens chrome does mount the Export menu for the lens — but a creator's worlds never reached it: world drafts live in STATE.worldCreatorLens.drafts, a per-user Map, and the shared export's state leg cannot see inside a Map value, so the export carried artifacts and DTUs only, never the worlds themselves. world-creator.js now registers a lens export provider emitting the caller's drafts at full fidelity — name, description, universeType, template, biome, visibility, publishedWorldId, rules, terrain, props, spawnPoints, zones, npcs, factions — scoped by the store's own per-user buckets (another creator's drafts never appear; anonymous callers get none). Suite server/tests/world-creator-export-provider.test.js 4/4; the pristine domain file fails the two positive pins.

The Healthcare export offered only the lens-wide bundle, so a single patient's record could not be exported without bulk data. PatientChartPanel already loads exactly one patient's complete chart via healthcare/patients-detail (patient + problems, allergies, vitals, labs, immunizations, encounters, photoNotes); the chart header now carries an Export patient chart control beside Edit patient that downloads that loaded chart — and only that chart — as patient-chart-<mrn>.json. No new fetch and no server change: the payload is the panel's own loaded detail, so it cannot contain another patient's data. Suite concord-frontend/tests/patient-chart-export.test.tsx 2/2 (payload shape + click-to-download); the pristine panel fails both pins; eslint clean.

The Creative Writing per-page CSV export dropped the writing itself: the JSON export is project-get's result verbatim (project.body is the manuscript prose, scenes carry their own body), but the hand-rolled CSV serializer emitted neither — the scene shape listed id/title/chapterId/order/wordCount/status and the project shape id/title/genre/targetWords/wordCount/timestamps. The serializer is now an exported buildPageCsv that appends a body column in both shapes (project.body for the single-row shape, scene.body per scene), with the page's existing csvCell quoting multiline prose safely. Suite concord-frontend/tests/creative-writing-csv-body.test.tsx 3/3, including the ticket's qa5 shape (project with body, no scenes); the pristine page fails all three pins; eslint clean.

The careers export that dumped 208 site-wide records reflected the pre-fix export; the shared scoping fixes (2026-11-10, FIX-feed-001) already keep the generic legs inside the lens and the caller. What was still missing was the lens's own data: a player's contracts live in the career_contracts table and their ladder/shift standing in player_career_progress, both behind the careers.* macros and invisible to every export leg, so the export carried artifacts and DTUs but never the careers data the ticket names (shifts, contracts, ladder). careers.js now registers a lens export provider emitting the caller's contracts (type 'contract': trackId, tier, role, baseWageSparks, payModel, durationDays, signingBonusSparks, status, the caller's role as worker or employer, the counterparty's kind — the counterparty's raw id is never an export field) and their per-track progress (type 'track-progress': tier, xp, highestTier, shifts, lastShiftDay), gated exactly like the domain itself (feature flag, db, authenticated actor). Suite server/tests/careers-export-provider.test.js 5/5 hermetic on the migrations' own table shapes; the pristine domain file fails the positive pins. Held in the local stack under the founder's 2026-11-13 batch-and-hold restatement; lands with the section push at SECTION DONE.

Three legs. (a) CSV fields: the shared serializer (9b6339511) already unions row data into CSV columns — the columns were empty because the lens's real records never reached the rows. (b) Workbench items: fields and scouting pins live in STATE.agricultureLens as nested per-user Maps (fields: userId -> fieldId -> field; scouts: userId -> pins), which the export's state leg cannot enumerate. agriculture.js now registers a lens export provider emitting the caller's fields (name, acreage, lat/lng, soilType, currentCrop — the ticket's missing columns), their scouting pins, and any rotation seasons the store holds, all scoped by the store's own per-user buckets. (c) No .dtu control: the agriculture page's header now mounts the shared DTUExportButton (domain 'agriculture', data fallback), whose export read now returns those provider rows. Server suite server/tests/agriculture-export-provider.test.js 5/5; the pristine domain file fails the positive pins; the page change lints clean and mounts the already-pinned shared button component. The photography export already had a provider (rolls via listShoots, the memory + restart-durable DB merge), and the shared serializer already unions data columns — the remainder was the frames: listShoots' frame projection carried only id/filename/mediaId/mimeType/fileSize, so a roll's photos exported without their URLs or any photo metadata, and the refs existed only nested inside roll rows where a CSV reader cannot use them (the ticket's 'CSV lacks photo refs, mixes rolls with DTUs' residue). listShoots now composes each frame with its URL (/api/media/<mediaId>/stream, the frontend's own pattern) and the photo record's metadata — camera, lens, ISO, aperture, shutter, focal length, dimensions, capture date, rating, flag, colour label, keywords (DB-durable frames keep nulls for EXIF, which that table deliberately never stored) — and the export provider additionally emits one flat photography_frame row per frame (rollId, rollName, filename, mediaId, url, mime, size, EXIF) alongside the roll rows, so CSV exports get real photo-ref columns. Suite server/tests/photography-export-frames.test.js 3/3 incl. the DB-only roll; the pristine domain file fails the content pins.
